analysis.title: Global Weekly Kickstart: Europe: A Different Route to AI
key_insights: Global equities fell 2.7% last week and Europe was the only region to stay positive. Technology fell 8.3% amid deleveraging of crowded AI positions.
Falling oil prices weighed on Energy (-10.2%), with Brent down 16.4%. Gold rose 4.3%.
GS Risk Appetite Indicator kept falling and Momentum saw a substantial unwind.

Europe offers diversification as scrutiny shifts from AI spending to returns. AI Infrastructure contributes 2pp of the STOXX 600's expected 9% earnings growth in 2027, while the S&P 500 is three times more sensitive to the AI factor.

Infrastructure remains attractive but needs more selectivity as capex growth peaks. Europe's AI Phase 2 screen has fallen 14% from its summer high, cutting its forward P/E from 23x to 18x, despite consensus expecting 20% EPS growth in 2027.
The next opportunity is in monetisation and productivity. European Software has de-rated despite resilient fundamentals.

GS's long-term AI beneficiaries screen implies c.45% potential EPS upside for companies with substantial exposure to AI automation. The scale and timing of the gains remain uncertain, alongside implementation risks.
GS 12-month index targets: S&P 500 8700 (from 7377, +17.9%), STOXX 600 695 (from 648, +7.2%), MSCI APxJ 1040 (+33.1%), Topix 4600 (+24.1%).
GS forecasts the US 10Y at 4.4% in 12 months from 4.9% now. Brent is forecast at $80 in 12 months from $98.3, and gold at $4620 from $4064.
Consensus bottom-up 2027 EPS growth: S&P 500 16%, STOXX 600 8%, TOPIX 13%, MXAPJ 30%. GS top-down estimates are 11%, 7%, 10% and 25%.
Consensus 2027E EPS growth is 8.3% for the STOXX 600 against 16.5% for the S&P 500. IT sector 2027E EPS growth is 44.8%.
The GS Bull/Bear Market Indicator is at 67%. The Shiller PE is at the 96th percentile and unemployment at the 82nd.
Valuation: 12m forward P/E is 17.9 for the US, 15.2 for AC World, 13.8 for Europe and 13.6 for Japan. The US ex Big Tech P/E is 17.0.
Week ahead: US CPI report and many Fed speakers. Europe has final October inflation, UK Q3 GDP and the Euro Area second GDP estimate. China releases October trade, PPI, CPI and credit data.
